correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=5, selected two-subsets correspond bijectively to K_n edges. The degree identity q(uv)=k-d(u)-d(v)+1_{uv selected} is verified by inclusion-exclusion, excludes sizes 1..3 and classifies four-edge ordinary forts via possible max degrees. Only four-stars, four-cycles, four-matchings and the exceptional n=6 claw-plus-edge survive; the last two ordinary-only types are rejected by inside-vertex skew neighbor counts. Counts follow uniquely from centers, 4-subsets, 8-point pairings and the exceptional 6*10 construction. Static enumeration through n=10 and independent dynamic forcing on n<=8 match every case, but the unrestricted theorem relies on the structural proof.

originality.rationale: The 2019 Kneser result gives the minimum SUCCESSFUL skew forcing number, not a maximum failed-seed census. The 2022 failed-skew result classifies graphs with failed-skew number one. The 2024 Kneser failed-zero-forcing scalar is explicitly credited and supplies no verified full minimum-fort or skew census; its full text is an access risk. The precise simultaneous classification (four-stars, four-cycles, four-matchings and exceptional six-vertex claws) and two count formulas were not covered by accessible prior statements. Research-record searches returned related but non-implicative results on skew failure in threshold graphs and forts of other graph families. Priority remains subject to external checking.

value.rationale: The count of maximum failed sets is a natural representation-independent measurement of how many extremal forcing obstructions occur. Exact dual ordinary/skew enumeration in canonical KG(n,2) reveals a structural distinction not captured by the established scalar equality of failed numbers. The cycle-only obstruction, onset of matchings at n=8, and n=6 exception explain meaningful nontrivial thresholds; the result is a full infinite-family classification, not a finite table or routine parameter renaming.
